feed.title: Straightedge blog
feed.subtitle: Mechanisms simulated, asserted, and animated from the simulation.

entry.title: The picture cannot show a state the algorithm did not reach
entry.summary: Twenty graph algorithms — BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, Bellman–Ford, Kruskal, Prim, topological sort, strongly connected components, max flow with its min cut, greedy colouring, bipartite matching with König's cover, Euler circuits, low-link connectivity, Prüfer codes, tree centres, ear decompositions, Gale–Shapley, Hamiltonian search, edge colouring, degeneracy orderings — computed once and drawn as SVG storyboard, five of them as Manim video too. A graph that makes the claim false is refused with the witness.

entry.title: Fourteen more algorithms, each with the witness it refuses on
entry.summary: A 34-module graph-theory course left a marker wherever the figure it wanted did not exist. Fourteen of those were algorithms — Prüfer codes, Gale–Shapley, Havel–Hakimi, Floyd–Warshall, Hamiltonian search, Turán and Mycielski constructions, edge colouring and more. 0.8.0 draws all of them from the computation and refuses, with the witness, what the graph makes false.

entry.title: The picture is not the proof
entry.summary: 1.618 is not the golden ratio, and every diagram tool that measures its own drawing says it is. Straightedge computes ruler-and-compass constructions in exact arithmetic, so a claim about a figure is decided rather than estimated.

entry.title: Matrix multiplication, four ways
entry.summary: AB is taught as a rule for filling in entries. Three other readings of the same product — by column, by row, and as a sum of rank-1 terms — explain what a matrix product is for, and two of them are what a systolic array and tensor parallelism already execute.

entry.title: Why the systolic array feeds itself diagonally
entry.summary: The diagonal in a systolic array is not a drawing convention. Entries entering on cycle t are exactly the anti-diagonal m + k = t, because that is the only arrival time at which a multiply meets the running sum it belongs to.

entry.title: Ring all-reduce: the bytes per rank don't grow
entry.summary: A ring all-reduce moves 2(N-1)/N times the buffer per rank — under 2D at every ring size, 1.5D at four ranks and 1.97D at sixty-four. Adding ranks does not cost bytes. What grows is the number of serial round trips.

entry.title: The pipeline bubble 1F1B doesn't fix
entry.summary: GPipe and 1F1B finish on the same cycle and idle for the same number of stage-slots. What 1F1B changes is activation memory — 23 sets against 6 — and that is the trade that decides whether a model fits.
